intended_object: The monoid of nonzero integral ideals I of 𝓞_K that are coprime to the modulus m = ∏_{P∈t} P, i.e. those with gcd(N(I), m) = 1. This is the integral part of the group I_K^m from class field theory, and genus characters are defined on it. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation (Cox §3.B).
explanation:
The carrier is the set of I ∈ (Ideal 𝓞_K)⁰ with IsCoprime (absNorm I : ℤ) (∏_{P∈t} P). Since the absolute norm is multiplicative and absNorm 1 = 1, this set is closed under multiplication and contains 1, so it is a submonoid.

Requiring gcd(N(I), m) = 1 is the standard way to say that I is coprime to m𝓞_K: every prime factor 𝔭 of I has norm a power of the rational prime p below it, so N(I) is coprime to m exactly when no prime factor of I lies above a prime dividing m. Any integer modulus can be written as a product over a finset (for example t = {m}), so the parametrization by t loses nothing.

The construction needs Ideal.absNorm, which requires finite residue rings, so a number field (or its ring of integers) is the natural setting for this object. Mathlib has no dedicated submonoid of ideals coprime to a modulus. Degenerate cases also behave correctly: if t is empty the modulus is 1 and every ideal qualifies; if 0 ∈ t the modulus is 0 and only the unit ideal (norm 1) qualifies, which is consistent with IsCoprime.
